facts.fact: Formally established 1892; the club calls itself 'The Oldest Golf Course West of the Mississippi River'.
More than 100 Roosevelt elk were counted on the course in 2017; the club tried coyote decoys to move them on.
The developer chose the shipwreck over a beer stein (2026-10-20).

current.subject: A wooden sailing ship, wrecked and half sunk.
current.keep: The wreck: the Clatsop coast's 'graveyard of the Pacific' story.
current.weaknesses: A busy little ship scene; the torn sail and waves blur at 1x.

concepts.name: The Wreck on the Beach
concepts.rationale: The rusted bow and ribs of an iron barque, half buried in the sand at the surf line: a skeleton you can read from across a room.
concepts.symbolism: Time and the sea: a course that has been here since 1892.
concepts.interpretation: It recalls the Peter Iredale wreck on Clatsop Spit, north of Gearhart; it is not a drawing of it.
concepts.tradeoffs: Shipwrecks are a coast-wide motif; reads as ruin more than golf.

concepts.name: The Gallery
concepts.rationale: A Roosevelt elk bull, front on: antlers, dark mane, long face. Gearhart's most faithful regulars are the herd that grazes its fairways.
concepts.symbolism: The locals who never pay dues: wild Oregon walking the oldest links in the West.
concepts.strengths: True, funny and very Gearhart; a strong frontal icon.
concepts.tradeoffs: Elk heads are common in lodge and hunting graphics; the joke needs the story.

recommendation: Concept 2. The elk is the most surprising true story in the set; the wreck stays a strong alternative.
